<a id="pagination"></a>

## Pagination

Page navigation with previous/next, collapsing ranges, and buttons or links.

- Install: `npx @grenishrai/expressive add pagination`
- Group: Navigation
- Files: `components/pagination.tsx`
- Expressive dependencies: `utils`, `styles`
- npm dependencies: none
- Docs: https://expressive.grenishrai.pro/docs/components/pagination

Pagination moves through pages of results. The current page is a tonal pill, and long ranges collapse into ellipses around it. Pages are buttons by default; pass `getHref` to make them links, which suits pages people share or open in new tabs.

### Usage

```tsx
import { Pagination } from "@/components/expressive/pagination";

<Pagination page={page} pageCount={20} onPageChange={setPage} />

// As links
<Pagination page={page} pageCount={20} getHref={(n) => `?page=${n}`} />
```

### Props

**Pagination**

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `page` | `number` |  | Current page, 1-based. |
| `pageCount` | `number` |  | Total pages. |
| `onPageChange` | `(page: number) => void` |  | Called when a page is chosen. |
| `getHref` | `(page: number) => string` |  | Render pages as links to these URLs. |
| `siblingCount` | `number` | `1` | Pages shown on each side of the current one. |
| `labels` | `{ previous?, next?, page? }` |  | Accessible labels, for translation. |
| `aria-label` | `string` | `"Pagination"` | Name of the navigation landmark. |

### Accessibility

- A `<nav>` landmark; every control is labelled ("Page 4", "Next page"), and the current page has `aria-current="page"`.
- Previous and next disable at the ends; ellipses are hidden from screen readers.

### Notes

- `paginationRange(page, pageCount, siblingCount)` is exported if you want the same page list in your own layout.

<a id="sidebar"></a>

## Sidebar

App sidebar that collapses to an icon rail or off-canvas, becomes a drawer on phones, and toggles with ⌘B.

- Install: `npx @grenishrai/expressive add sidebar`
- Group: Navigation
- Files: `components/sidebar.tsx`
- Expressive dependencies: `utils`, `motion`, `icon-button`, `tooltip`, `styles`
- npm dependencies: `@base-ui/react`
- Docs: https://expressive.grenishrai.pro/docs/components/sidebar

The sidebar is the persistent side panel of an app layout: a header, scrolling navigation in groups, and a footer. On wide screens it collapses to an 80px icon rail, where labels become tooltips and the active indicator matches the navigation rail, or slides away entirely. Three looks: flush to the edge, a floating card, or inset, where the main area becomes the card. Below 768px it becomes a modal drawer you can swipe closed. ⌘B or Ctrl+B toggles it, and the expanded state is remembered. For Material's standalone patterns, see the navigation rail and navigation drawer.

### Usage

```tsx
import Link from "next/link";
import {
  Sidebar, SidebarContent, SidebarFooter, SidebarGroup, SidebarHeader, SidebarInset,
  SidebarMenu, SidebarMenuButton, SidebarMenuItem, SidebarProvider, SidebarTrigger,
} from "@/components/expressive/sidebar";

export default function Layout({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) {
  return (
    <SidebarProvider>
      <Sidebar>
        <SidebarHeader><Logo /></SidebarHeader>
        <SidebarContent>
          <SidebarGroup label="Mail">
            <SidebarMenu>
              <SidebarMenuItem>
                <SidebarMenuButton render={<Link href="/inbox" />} icon={<InboxIcon />} badge="24" active>
                  Inbox
                </SidebarMenuButton>
              </SidebarMenuItem>
            </SidebarMenu>
          </SidebarGroup>
          <SidebarGroup label="Labels" collapsible>…</SidebarGroup>
        </SidebarContent>
        <SidebarFooter><Account /></SidebarFooter>
      </Sidebar>
      <SidebarInset>
        <header><SidebarTrigger /></header>
        {children}
      </SidebarInset>
    </SidebarProvider>
  );
}
```

### Props

**SidebarProvider**

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `defaultOpen` | `boolean` | `true` | Expanded on wide screens when nothing is remembered yet. |
| `open / onOpenChange` | `boolean` |  | Control the wide-screen state. |
| `storageKey` | `string \| null` | `"expressive:sidebar"` | Where the state is remembered (localStorage); `null` turns it off. |
| `keyboardShortcut` | `string \| false` | `"b"` | Toggle with ⌘ / Ctrl and this key; ignored while typing in a field. |
| `width / collapsedWidth` | `string` | `"18rem" / "5rem"` | Expanded and icon-rail widths. |

**Sidebar**

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `collapsible` | `"icon" \| "offcanvas" \| "none"` | `"icon"` | Collapse to an icon rail, slide away, or stay put. |
| `variant` | `"standard" \| "floating" \| "inset"` | `"standard"` | `standard`: flush to the edge. `floating`: the sidebar is a rounded card. `inset`: the sidebar blends into the page and `SidebarInset` becomes a raised rounded card beside it. |
| `side` | `"left" \| "right"` | `"left"` | Which edge it sits on (and swipes toward on phones). |
| `aria-label` | `string` | `"Sidebar"` | Names the drawer on narrow screens. |

**SidebarMenuButton**

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `href / render` | `string / ReactElement` |  | A link (your router's `Link` via `render`), or `render={<button type="button" />}` for an action. |
| `icon / activeIcon` | `ReactNode` |  | Icon, and an optional filled one for the active state. |
| `active` | `boolean` |  | The current page: indicator and `aria-current="page"`. |
| `badge` | `ReactNode` |  | Trailing text such as a count; a dot in the icon rail. |
| `tooltip` | `string` |  | Tooltip in the icon rail. Defaults to the label when it's text. |

**SidebarGroup**

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | `ReactNode` |  | Section title, hidden in the icon rail. |
| `collapsible / defaultOpen` | `boolean` |  | Open and close the section from its title. The icon rail always shows its items. |
| `action` | `ReactNode` |  | Something after the title, like an add button. |

**useSidebar()**

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `open / setOpen` |  |  | Wide-screen state. |
| `openMobile / setOpenMobile` |  |  | The drawer on narrow screens. |
| `toggle()` |  |  | Toggles whichever applies to the current width. |

**Other parts**

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `SidebarHeader / SidebarFooter` |  |  | Fixed top and bottom areas. |
| `SidebarContent` |  |  | The scrolling middle, rendered as the `<nav>` landmark (`aria-label` defaults to "Main"). |
| `SidebarMenuSub / SidebarMenuSubButton` |  |  | Nested destinations, hidden in the icon rail. |
| `SidebarTrigger` |  |  | The toggle button (an IconButton). |
| `SidebarInset` |  |  | The `<main>` area beside the sidebar; a raised rounded card with the `inset` variant. |
| `useSidebarRail()` |  |  | Whether this sidebar is the icon rail. For header and footer content, prefer fading text with `group-data-[collapsible=icon]/sidebar:opacity-0` and keeping icons 40px from the edge, so nothing jumps. |

### Accessibility

- The menu is a `<nav>` landmark of links; the current one has `aria-current="page"`.
- In the icon rail, labels stay in each link's accessible name and show as tooltips on hover and focus.
- When an off-canvas sidebar slides away it becomes `inert`, so Tab skips it.
- On narrow screens it's a modal drawer: focus is trapped, Escape or a swipe closes it, and focus returns to the trigger.
- The trigger reports `aria-expanded`; the shortcut is ignored in text fields, where ⌘B means bold.

### Notes

- The wide/narrow switch is Tailwind's `md` breakpoint (768px).
- Collapsing never moves an icon: items keep their layout and shrink to a 56px pill around it, labels fade, and group titles and sub-items fold away. Line up your own header and footer icons 40px from the edge (12px of `SidebarHeader` padding plus 12px of your own) to match.
- The remembered state is restored after hydration, so a server-rendered page can briefly show the default. Pass `open` from a cookie if you need it exact on first paint.

<a id="tabs"></a>

## Tabs

Primary and secondary tabs, fixed or scrollable, with a springy indicator.

- Install: `npx @grenishrai/expressive add tabs`
- Group: Navigation
- Files: `components/tabs.tsx`
- Expressive dependencies: `utils`, `motion`, `styles`
- npm dependencies: `@base-ui/react`
- Docs: https://expressive.grenishrai.pro/docs/components/tabs

Tabs organise content into views at the same level. Primary tabs sit under a top app bar, with an indicator that hugs the label; secondary tabs divide one area further, with an indicator that spans the tab. The indicator springs from tab to tab. Make the row `scrollable` past four or five tabs.

### Usage

```tsx
import { Tab, Tabs, TabsList, TabsPanel } from "@/components/expressive/tabs";

<Tabs defaultValue="photos">
  <TabsList aria-label="Library">
    <Tab value="photos" icon={<ImageIcon />}>Photos</Tab>
    <Tab value="albums" icon={<FolderIcon />}>Albums</Tab>
  </TabsList>
  <TabsPanel value="photos">…</TabsPanel>
  <TabsPanel value="albums">…</TabsPanel>
</Tabs>
```

### Props

**Tabs**

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `value / defaultValue` | `string \| number` |  | The active tab (controlled / uncontrolled). |
| `onValueChange` | `(value) => void` |  | Called when the active tab changes. |

**TabsList**

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `variant` | `"primary" \| "secondary"` | `"primary"` | Label-width or full-width indicator, and the active color. |
| `scrollable` | `boolean` | `false` | Scroll sideways, with tabs sized to their labels. |
| `activateOnFocus` | `boolean` | `false` | Switch tabs as arrow keys move focus, rather than on Enter or Space. |
| `motion` | `"expressive" \| "standard" \| "fluid" \| "none"` | `theme default` | Motion scheme for this component's transitions. `none` turns animation off. |

**Tab**

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `value` | `string \| number` |  | Matches a `TabsPanel`. |
| `icon` | `ReactNode` |  | Above the label in primary tabs, beside it in secondary tabs. |
| `badge` | `ReactNode` |  | A `<Badge>`, pinned to the icon (or after the label without one). |
| `disabled` | `boolean` |  | Disables the tab. |

### Accessibility

- Base UI's tabs: `role="tablist"`, `tab` and `tabpanel`, with `aria-selected` and `aria-controls` wired up.
- Arrow keys move between tabs; Enter or Space activates one (or pass `activateOnFocus`).
- Give the `TabsList` an `aria-label` when nothing else names it.

<a id="toolbar"></a>

## Toolbar

Floating and docked toolbars, standard or vibrant, with arrow-key navigation.

- Install: `npx @grenishrai/expressive add toolbar`
- Group: Navigation
- Files: `components/toolbar.tsx`
- Expressive dependencies: `utils`, `icon-button`, `styles`
- npm dependencies: `@base-ui/react`
- Docs: https://expressive.grenishrai.pro/docs/components/toolbar

Toolbars hold actions for the current page. The floating toolbar is a pill that sits over content, horizontally or vertically, often next to a FAB; the docked toolbar spans the bottom of the window. `vibrant` swaps the surface for primary-container colors.

### Usage

```tsx
import { IconButton, ToggleIconButton } from "@/components/expressive/icon-button";
import { Toolbar, ToolbarButton, ToolbarSeparator } from "@/components/expressive/toolbar";

<Toolbar aria-label="Formatting">
  <ToolbarButton render={<IconButton aria-label="Undo" />}><UndoIcon /></ToolbarButton>
  <ToolbarSeparator />
  <ToolbarButton render={<ToggleIconButton aria-label="Bold" />}><BoldIcon /></ToolbarButton>
</Toolbar>
```

### Props

**Toolbar**

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `variant` | `"floating" \| "docked"` | `"floating"` | A pill over content, or a full-width bar. |
| `color` | `"standard" \| "vibrant"` | `"standard"` | Surface or primary-container colors. |
| `orientation` | `"horizontal" \| "vertical"` | `"horizontal"` | Layout, and which arrow keys move focus. |
| `aria-label` | `string` |  | Name for the toolbar. |
| `className` | `string` |  | Extra classes, merged with tailwind-merge. |

**ToolbarButton**

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `render` | `ReactElement` |  | The control to use, usually an `IconButton` or `ToggleIconButton`. |

**ToolbarSeparator**

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `orientation` | `"horizontal" \| "vertical"` |  | Defaults to the opposite of the toolbar's. |

### Accessibility

- Renders `role="toolbar"`: the whole toolbar is one tab stop, and arrow keys move between its items.
- Disabled items stay focusable by default so keyboard users can still find them.

### Notes

- Standard icon buttons inside pick up the toolbar's colors (including selected toggles); filled and tonal ones keep their own, so use one to highlight the key action.

<a id="top-app-bar"></a>

## Top app bar

Small, center-aligned, medium and large top app bars that tint on scroll.

- Install: `npx @grenishrai/expressive add top-app-bar`
- Group: Navigation
- Files: `components/top-app-bar.tsx`
- Expressive dependencies: `utils`, `styles`
- npm dependencies: none
- Docs: https://expressive.grenishrai.pro/docs/components/top-app-bar

The top app bar shows the screen's title, navigation and key actions. Small and center-aligned bars are 64px tall; medium and large flexible bars give the title more room below the actions. The bar tints to surface-container once content scrolls under it.

### Usage

```tsx
import { TopAppBar } from "@/components/expressive/top-app-bar";

<TopAppBar
  variant="medium"
  title="Inbox"
  subtitle="3 unread"
  navigation={<IconButton aria-label="Menu"><MenuIcon /></IconButton>}
  actions={<IconButton aria-label="Search"><SearchIcon /></IconButton>}
/>
```

### Props

**TopAppBar**

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | `ReactNode` |  | Rendered as the page `<h1>`. |
| `subtitle` | `ReactNode` |  | Secondary line. |
| `variant` | `"small" \| "center" \| "medium" \| "large"` | `"small"` | Layout and title size. |
| `navigation` | `ReactNode` |  | Leading slot (menu or back button). |
| `actions` | `ReactNode` |  | Trailing slot, up to three icon buttons. |
| `scrolled` | `boolean` |  | Force the scrolled tint. By default it follows the scroll position. |
| `scrollTarget` | `RefObject<HTMLElement>` | `window` | Scroll container to watch. |

### Accessibility

- Renders a `<header>` with the title as an `<h1>`.
- Every icon button in the slots needs its own accessible name.

### Notes

- Medium and large bars don't collapse their title on scroll yet; they only tint.

<a id="accordion"></a>

## Accordion

Expandable sections, segmented or divided, with springy panels.

- Install: `npx @grenishrai/expressive add accordion`
- Group: Containment
- Files: `components/accordion.tsx`
- Expressive dependencies: `utils`, `motion`, `styles`
- npm dependencies: `@base-ui/react`
- Docs: https://expressive.grenishrai.pro/docs/components/accordion

Accordions stack sections that expand to show their content: FAQs, settings groups, long forms in steps. The `segmented` style matches Expressive's segmented lists, with each section its own tile that grows rounder corners when open; `divided` separates rows with lines. Panels spring open on the motion tokens.

### Usage

```tsx
import { Accordion, AccordionItem, AccordionPanel, AccordionTrigger } from "@/components/expressive/accordion";

<Accordion defaultValue={["shipping"]}>
  <AccordionItem value="shipping">
    <AccordionTrigger icon={<TruckIcon />}>Shipping</AccordionTrigger>
    <AccordionPanel>Orders ship within two working days.</AccordionPanel>
  </AccordionItem>
  <AccordionItem value="returns">
    <AccordionTrigger supportingText="Free for 30 days">Returns</AccordionTrigger>
    <AccordionPanel>Print the label from your order page.</AccordionPanel>
  </AccordionItem>
</Accordion>
```

### Props

**Accordion**

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `variant` | `"segmented" \| "divided"` | `"segmented"` | Separate rounded tiles, or rows divided by lines. |
| `value / defaultValue` | `unknown[]` |  | Open sections (controlled / uncontrolled). |
| `onValueChange` | `(value) => void` |  | Called when sections open or close. |
| `multiple` | `boolean` | `false` | Allow several sections open at once. |
| `hiddenUntilFound` | `boolean` | `false` | Let the browser's find-in-page search closed panels and open them. |
| `motion` | `"expressive" \| "standard" \| "fluid" \| "none"` | `theme default` | Motion scheme for this component's transitions. `none` turns animation off. |

**AccordionItem**

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `value` | `unknown` |  | Identifies the section in the accordion's value. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` |  | Disables the section. |

**AccordionTrigger**

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `icon` | `ReactNode` |  | Leading icon. |
| `supportingText` | `ReactNode` |  | Smaller text under the title. |

### Accessibility

- Each trigger is a button inside a heading, with `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls`; the panel is a labelled region.
- Enter or Space toggles a section; Tab moves between headers (the ARIA guidance no longer recommends arrow keys here).
- Panels animate on spring tokens and snap open under reduced motion.

<a id="avatar"></a>

## Avatar

Images with initials fallback, in five sizes, as circles or any Material shape, plus avatar groups.

- Install: `npx @grenishrai/expressive add avatar`
- Group: Containment
- Files: `components/avatar.tsx`
- Expressive dependencies: `utils`, `material-shapes`, `styles`
- npm dependencies: `@base-ui/react`
- Docs: https://expressive.grenishrai.pro/docs/components/avatar

Avatars show a person or entity: a photo, falling back to initials while it loads or if it fails. Five sizes, four fallback colors, and besides the circle, any of the 35 Material shapes, one of M3 Expressive's signature details. `AvatarGroup` overlaps several and collapses the rest into "+N".

### Usage

```tsx
import { Avatar, AvatarGroup } from "@/components/expressive/avatar";

<Avatar src={user.photo} alt={user.name} />
<Avatar alt="Ada Lovelace" size="lg" shape="cookie-9" color="tertiary" />

<AvatarGroup max={4} aria-label="Project members">
  {members.map((m) => <Avatar key={m.id} src={m.photo} alt={m.name} />)}
</AvatarGroup>
```

### Props

**Avatar**

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `alt` | `string` |  | Required: the person's or entity's name. Used as alt text and for initials. |
| `src` | `string` |  | Image URL. |
| `fallback` | `ReactNode` |  | Shown instead of initials, e.g. an icon. |
| `size` | `"xs" \| "sm" \| "md" \| "lg" \| "xl"` | `"md"` | 24, 32, 40, 56 or 96px. |
| `shape` | `MaterialShapeName` | `"circle"` | Circle or any Material shape (`"cookie-9"`, `"clover-4"`, `"flower"`…). |
| `color` | `"primary" \| "secondary" \| "tertiary" \| "surface"` | `"primary"` | Fallback colors. |
| `className` | `string` |  | Extra classes, merged with tailwind-merge. |

**AvatarGroup**

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `max` | `number` |  | Show at most this many; the rest become "+N". |
| `size` | `Avatar size` | `"md"` | Size of the "+N" avatar; match the avatars. |
| `aria-label` | `string` |  | Names the group. |

### Accessibility

- The image uses `alt`; the initials fallback is `role="img"` named by `alt`, with the letters hidden from screen readers.
- The "+N" avatar is announced as "N more".
- Next to the person's visible name the avatar repeats it; to keep it quiet there, add `aria-hidden` to the avatar.

<a id="bottom-sheet"></a>

## Bottom sheet

Modal bottom sheet with a drag handle, swipe to dismiss and snap points.

- Install: `npx @grenishrai/expressive add bottom-sheet`
- Group: Containment
- Files: `components/bottom-sheet.tsx`
- Expressive dependencies: `utils`, `motion`, `styles`
- npm dependencies: `@base-ui/react`
- Docs: https://expressive.grenishrai.pro/docs/components/bottom-sheet

Bottom sheets show secondary content anchored to the bottom of the screen, like share targets or a list of options. The sheet springs up over a scrim; drag the handle down to dismiss it. With `snapPoints` it rests at a partial height and drags up to full height.

### Usage

```tsx
import {
  BottomSheet,
  BottomSheetContent,
  BottomSheetTitle,
  BottomSheetTrigger,
} from "@/components/expressive/bottom-sheet";

<BottomSheet snapPoints={["20rem", 1]}>
  <BottomSheetTrigger render={<Button variant="tonal" />}>Share</BottomSheetTrigger>
  <BottomSheetContent>
    <BottomSheetTitle>Share to</BottomSheetTitle>
    …
  </BottomSheetContent>
</BottomSheet>
```

### Props

**BottomSheet**

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `open / defaultOpen / onOpenChange` | `boolean` |  | Control the sheet. |
| `snapPoints` | `Array<number \| string>` |  | Resting heights: fractions of the viewport (0–1), pixels, or `"20rem"`. |
| `snapPoint / onSnapPointChange` | `number \| string` |  | Control the current snap point. |
| `modal` | `boolean` | `true` | Trap focus and lock page scroll while open. |

**BottomSheetContent**

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `handle` | `boolean` | `true` | Show the drag handle. |
| `motion` | `"expressive" \| "standard" \| "fluid" \| "none"` | `theme default` | Motion scheme for this component's transitions. `none` turns animation off. |
| `className` | `string` |  | Extra classes, merged with tailwind-merge. |

### Accessibility

- Opens as a modal `dialog`: focus moves inside and stays there, and Escape or a tap on the scrim closes it.
- Name it with `BottomSheetTitle` (wired to `aria-labelledby`).
- Dragging is optional: everything it does is also possible with the keyboard.

<a id="card"></a>

## Card

Elevated, filled and outlined cards, optionally interactive.

- Install: `npx @grenishrai/expressive add card`
- Group: Containment
- Files: `components/card.tsx`
- Expressive dependencies: `utils`, `styles`
- npm dependencies: `@base-ui/react`, `class-variance-authority`
- Docs: https://expressive.grenishrai.pro/docs/components/card

Cards group content and actions about a single subject. Elevated cards separate themselves with a shadow, filled cards with a stronger surface, outlined cards with a border. Make the whole card a link or button with `interactive` and `render`.

### Usage

```tsx
import { Card, CardContent, CardDescription, CardHeader, CardTitle } from "@/components/expressive/card";

<Card variant="outlined">
  <CardHeader>
    <CardTitle>Trip to Lisbon</CardTitle>
    <CardDescription>May 3–9</CardDescription>
  </CardHeader>
  <CardContent>Flights and hotel are booked.</CardContent>
</Card>

<Card interactive render={<a href="/trips/lisbon" />}>…</Card>
```

### Props

**Card**

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `variant` | `"elevated" \| "filled" \| "outlined"` | `"elevated"` | How the card separates from the page. |
| `shape` | `"small" \| "medium" \| "large" \| "extra-large" \| "squircle" \| "cut"` | `"medium"` | Corner shape. |
| `interactive` | `boolean` | `false` | Adds state layer, focus ring and press morph. |
| `render` | `ReactElement` |  | Element to render as, e.g. `<a href>` for a clickable card. |

**CardHeader, CardTitle, CardDescription, CardMedia, CardContent, CardActions**

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `…` | `div / h3 / p props` |  | Layout parts with the right spacing and type roles. |

### Accessibility

- A plain card is a `<div>`; it adds no semantics.
- For a clickable card, render it as a link or button so the whole surface is one focusable target, and avoid nesting other buttons inside it.

<a id="carousel"></a>

## Carousel

M3 carousel with snapping, masked edge items and parallax, in multi-browse, hero and uncontained layouts.

- Install: `npx @grenishrai/expressive add carousel`
- Group: Containment
- Files: `components/carousel.tsx`
- Expressive dependencies: `utils`, `motion`, `styles`
- npm dependencies: none
- Docs: https://expressive.grenishrai.pro/docs/components/carousel

Carousels show a row of visual items that scroll sideways and snap. In the `multi-browse` and `hero` layouts, items cut off at the edges are masked into rounded tiles and their content shifts as they move, M3's parallax, instead of being sliced by the edge. Native scrolling does the work, so touch, trackpads and the keyboard all feel right, and a mouse can drag the row. Scrolling stays at 60fps: item positions are measured once, and each frame only moves the masks and parallax layers.

### Usage

```tsx
import { Carousel, CarouselItem } from "@/components/expressive/carousel";

<Carousel aria-label="Destinations">
  {places.map((place) => (
    <CarouselItem key={place.id} label={place.name}>
      <img src={place.photo} alt={place.description} />
    </CarouselItem>
  ))}
</Carousel>
```

### Props

**Carousel**

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `aria-label` | `string` |  | Required: names the carousel. |
| `layout` | `"multi-browse" \| "hero" \| "uncontained"` | `"multi-browse"` | Item widths and snapping; `uncontained` skips the edge masking. |
| `height` | `string` | `"16rem"` | Item height. |
| `controls` | `boolean` | `true` | Previous and next buttons. |
| `labels` | `{ previous?, next?, slide? }` |  | Button labels and the slide name ("1 of 6"), for translation. |

**CarouselItem**

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | `ReactNode` |  | Text over the bottom of the item. |
| `children` | `ReactNode` |  | Usually an `<img>` or `<video>`; it fills the item. |

### Accessibility

- A region with `aria-roledescription="carousel"`; each item is a group announced as "slide, 1 of 6".
- The row is focusable, so arrow keys scroll it; the buttons scroll one item and disable at the ends.
- Mouse users can drag the row; a drag never activates a link or button inside an item, while a plain click still does.
- No autoplay: content only moves when the user moves it. Button scrolling is instant under reduced motion.

<a id="code-block"></a>

## Code block

Copyable code blocks and synced code tabs with icons, file names and line numbers; bring your own highlighter.

- Install: `npx @grenishrai/expressive add code-block`
- Group: Containment
- Files: `components/code-block.tsx`
- Expressive dependencies: `utils`, `styles`
- npm dependencies: none
- Docs: https://expressive.grenishrai.pro/docs/components/code-block

Code blocks show copyable snippets with an icon, file name, language label and optional line numbers. `CodeTabs` puts several snippets behind tabs, like one command per package manager or the files of an example, each tab with its own icon. Blocks that share a `syncKey` switch together and remember the choice, so picking pnpm once updates every install command on the page. Neither bundles a syntax highlighter: pass plain `code`, or `html` from one you already use (Shiki on the server works well).

### Usage

```tsx
import { CodeBlock, CodeTabs } from "@/components/expressive/code-block";

<CodeBlock code={source} title="button.tsx" language="tsx" lineNumbers />

<CodeTabs
  aria-label="Package manager"
  syncKey="package-manager"
  items={[
    { value: "npm", label: "npm", language: "bash", icon: <NpmLogo />, code: "npx @grenishrai/expressive init" },
    { value: "pnpm", label: "pnpm", language: "bash", icon: <PnpmLogo />, code: "pnpm dlx @grenishrai/expressive init" },
  ]}
/>

// Highlighted with Shiki (server component)
const html = await codeToHtml(source, { lang: "tsx", theme: "github-dark" });
<CodeBlock code={source} html={html} title="button.tsx" language="tsx" />
```

### Props

**CodeBlock**

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `code` | `string` |  | Required: the source. It's what the copy button copies. |
| `html` | `string` |  | Highlighted HTML (a `<pre>`). Only pass trusted HTML. |
| `title` | `ReactNode` |  | File name or caption in the header. |
| `language` | `string` |  | Label in the header (`tsx`, `bash`…); also picks the default icon. |
| `icon` | `ReactNode \| null` |  | Header icon. Defaults to one for the language; `null` hides it. |
| `lineNumbers` | `boolean` | `false` | Number each line (works with Shiki's `.line` spans). |
| `wrap` | `boolean` | `false` | Wrap long lines instead of scrolling. |
| `maxHeight` | `string` |  | Scroll vertically past this height. |
| `labels` | `{ copy?, copied? }` |  | Copy button labels, for translation. |

**CodeTabs**

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `items` | `CodeTab[]` |  | The tabs: `{ value, label, code, html?, language?, icon? }`. |
| `value / defaultValue` | `string` |  | The active tab (controlled / uncontrolled). |
| `onValueChange` | `(value: string) => void` |  | Called when the tab changes. |
| `syncKey` | `string` |  | Blocks with the same key switch together and remember the choice in localStorage. |
| `aria-label` | `string` | `"Code"` | Names the tab list, e.g. "Package manager". |
| `lineNumbers / wrap / maxHeight / labels` |  |  | As on CodeBlock, for every tab. |

**CodeTab**

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `value` | `string` |  | Unique id. With `syncKey`, tabs match across blocks by value (`"pnpm"`). |
| `label` | `ReactNode` |  | Tab text. |
| `icon` | `ReactNode \| null` |  | Tab icon, e.g. a brand logo. Defaults to one for `language`; `null` hides it. |
| `code / html / language` |  |  | The snippet, as on CodeBlock. |

### Accessibility

- CodeBlock is a `<figure>` with its header as the caption; CodeTabs is a real tab list (`role="tablist"`, arrow keys between tabs).
- The code area is focusable so keyboard users can scroll it.
- The copy button copies the visible tab, and "Copied" is announced through a live region.
- Icons are decorative (`aria-hidden`); the tab label carries the name. Line numbers are CSS, so screen readers and copy-paste skip them.

### Notes

- `CodeLanguageIcon` is exported: the built-in icons are a terminal for shell languages, braces for JSON, a page for Markdown and text, and code brackets for everything else.
- The synced choice is stored per `syncKey`; if storage is unavailable (private mode), blocks still sync on the page.

<a id="dialog"></a>

## Dialog

Modal dialog with focus trapping and spring enter/exit transitions.

- Install: `npx @grenishrai/expressive add dialog`
- Group: Containment
- Files: `components/dialog.tsx`
- Expressive dependencies: `utils`, `motion`, `styles`
- npm dependencies: `@base-ui/react`
- Docs: https://expressive.grenishrai.pro/docs/components/dialog

Dialogs interrupt to ask for a decision or show critical information. Keep them short: a title, one or two sentences, and at most two actions.

### Usage

```tsx
import {
  Dialog, DialogActions, DialogClose, DialogContent,
  DialogDescription, DialogTitle, DialogTrigger,
} from "@/components/expressive/dialog";

<Dialog>
  <DialogTrigger render={<Button variant="tonal" />}>Reset settings</DialogTrigger>
  <DialogContent>
    <DialogTitle>Reset settings?</DialogTitle>
    <DialogDescription>Your preferences go back to their defaults.</DialogDescription>
    <DialogActions>
      <DialogClose render={<Button variant="text" />}>Cancel</DialogClose>
      <DialogClose render={<Button variant="text" />} onClick={reset}>Reset</DialogClose>
    </DialogActions>
  </DialogContent>
</Dialog>
```

### Props

**Dialog**

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `open / defaultOpen` | `boolean` |  | Open state. |
| `onOpenChange` | `(open: boolean) => void` |  | Called on open and close. |
| `modal` | `boolean \| "trap-focus"` | `true` | Whether the rest of the page is inert. |

**DialogContent**

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `motion` | `"expressive" \| "standard" \| "fluid" \| "none"` | `theme default` | Motion scheme for this component's transitions. `none` turns animation off. |
| `className` | `string` |  | Extra classes, merged with tailwind-merge. |

**DialogTitle, DialogDescription, DialogIcon, DialogActions, DialogTrigger, DialogClose**

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `…` |  |  | Parts; Title and Description are wired to the dialog's `aria-labelledby` and `aria-describedby`. |

### Accessibility

- Focus moves into the dialog on open, is trapped while it's open, and returns to the trigger on close.
- Escape and clicking the scrim close it.
- Always include a DialogTitle so the dialog has an accessible name.

<a id="divider"></a>

## Divider

Horizontal and vertical dividers, full width or inset.

- Install: `npx @grenishrai/expressive add divider`
- Group: Containment
- Files: `components/divider.tsx`
- Expressive dependencies: `utils`, `styles`
- npm dependencies: `@base-ui/react`
- Docs: https://expressive.grenishrai.pro/docs/components/divider

Dividers are thin lines that group content in lists and layouts. Use them sparingly, where spacing alone doesn't separate groups clearly. Horizontal dividers can be inset from the leading edge or from both edges.

### Usage

```tsx
import { Divider } from "@/components/expressive/divider";

<Divider />
<Divider inset="middle" />
<div className="flex items-center gap-4">
  Edit <Divider orientation="vertical" /> View
</div>
```

### Props

**Divider**

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `orientation` | `"horizontal" \| "vertical"` | `"horizontal"` | Direction of the line. |
| `inset` | `"none" \| "start" \| "middle"` | `"none"` | `start` insets the leading edge by 16px; `middle` insets both ends. |
| `className` | `string` |  | Extra classes, merged with tailwind-merge. |

### Accessibility

- Renders `role="separator"` with `aria-orientation`.
- For a purely decorative line, a border on the surrounding element is enough.

<a id="list"></a>

## List

One-, two- and three-line lists with leading and trailing slots, standard or segmented.

- Install: `npx @grenishrai/expressive add list`
- Group: Containment
- Files: `components/list.tsx`
- Expressive dependencies: `utils`, `styles`
- npm dependencies: `@base-ui/react`
- Docs: https://expressive.grenishrai.pro/docs/components/list

Lists show a column of related items, each with a headline, optional overline and supporting text, and leading and trailing slots for icons, avatars, controls or short text. The `segmented` variant is the M3 Expressive look: each item is its own rounded tile, and selected items grow rounder corners.

### Usage

```tsx
import { List, ListItem } from "@/components/expressive/list";

<List aria-label="Mailboxes" variant="segmented">
  <ListItem headline="Inbox" leading={<InboxIcon />} trailing="24" render={<a href="/inbox" />} selected />
  <ListItem headline="Drafts" leading={<DraftIcon />} render={<a href="/drafts" />} />
</List>
```

### Props

**List**

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `variant` | `"standard" \| "segmented"` | `"standard"` | Plain rows, or separate rounded tiles. |

**ListItem**

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `headline` | `ReactNode` |  | The main text. |
| `overline` | `ReactNode` |  | Small text above the headline. |
| `supportingText` | `ReactNode` |  | Text below the headline; wraps to two lines. |
| `leading` | `ReactNode` |  | Icon, avatar or image before the text. |
| `trailing` | `ReactNode` |  | Icon, control or short text after the text. |
| `render` | `ReactElement` |  | Makes the item interactive: `<a href>`, your router's Link, or `<button>`. |
| `selected` | `boolean` |  | Selected state; sets `aria-current` on interactive items. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` |  | Dims the item and blocks pointer input. |
| `itemProps` | `ComponentProps<"li">` |  | Props for the `<li>` wrapper. |

### Accessibility

- Renders `<ul role="list">` and `<li>`, so screen readers announce the count.
- Interactive items are real links or buttons and get a focus ring; a control in the trailing slot needs its own label.

### Notes

- Don't put a link or button in the trailing slot of an interactive item: nested interactive elements confuse keyboard and screen reader users.

<a id="shape"></a>

## Shape

All 35 Material 3 Expressive shapes (flower, cookies, bursts, clovers…) that morph into each other.

- Install: `npx @grenishrai/expressive add shape`
- Group: Containment
- Files: `components/shape.tsx`
- Expressive dependencies: `material-shapes`, `motion`, `utils`, `styles`
- npm dependencies: none
- Docs: https://expressive.grenishrai.pro/docs/components/shape

The 35 shapes of Material 3 Expressive: cookies, clovers, bursts, the flower, puffy and pixel shapes, and more. Use them for avatars, image crops, decorative accents and loading states. Change `name` and the shape morphs into the new one on the motion scheme's spring.

### Usage

```tsx
import { Shape } from "@/components/expressive/shape";

<Shape name="flower" className="size-24 text-primary" />

// Morphs whenever the name changes
<Shape name={loading ? "soft-burst" : "cookie-9"} className="size-12 text-tertiary" />

// Clip anything to a shape with the Tailwind utilities
<img src={avatar} alt="" className="size-16 object-cover shape-cookie-12" />
```

### Props

**Shape**

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `MaterialShapeName` |  | One of 35 shapes, e.g. `flower`, `cookie-9`, `clover-4`, `soft-burst`, `heart`. |
| `label` | `string` |  | Accessible name. Without it the shape is decorative (`aria-hidden`). |
| `speed` | `"fast" \| "default" \| "slow"` | `"default"` | Spring speed of the morph. |
| `motion` | `"expressive" \| "standard" \| "fluid" \| "none"` | `theme default` | Motion scheme for this component's transitions. `none` turns animation off. |
| `className` | `string` |  | Size it with `size-*`; it fills with the text color (`text-*`). |

**shape-* utilities**

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `shape-{name}` | `Tailwind utility` |  | Masks any element to a shape, e.g. `shape-flower` on an `<img>`. Only the ones you use end up in your CSS. |
| `shapeMask(name)` | `(name) => string` |  | The same mask as a CSS value, from `tokens/material-shapes`. |

### Accessibility

- Shapes are decorative by default and hidden from screen readers.
- Give a meaningful shape a `label`; it then renders as `role="img"`.
- Morphs respect reduced motion: the shape switches instantly.

### Notes

- Generated from Jetpack Compose's MaterialShapes and androidx.graphics.shapes (Apache-2.0), so the geometry matches Android.
- Morphing samples both outlines and interpolates between them. Sharp shapes (the pixel ones) land on their exact outline when the morph ends.

## Side sheet

Modal side sheet from either edge, with header, scrolling body and actions.

- Install: `npx @grenishrai/expressive add side-sheet`
- Group: Containment

Side sheets show supplementary content, like filters or details, sliding in from the edge of the window over a scrim. They pair a header and scrolling body with an optional row of actions. Set `side="left"` to open from the left edge.

```tsx
  SideSheet,
  SideSheetActions,
  SideSheetBody,
  SideSheetClose,

  SideSheetHeader,
  SideSheetTitle,
  SideSheetTrigger,
} from "@/components/expressive/side-sheet";

<SideSheet>
  <SideSheetTrigger render={<Button variant="tonal" />}>Filters</SideSheetTrigger>
  <SideSheetContent>
    <SideSheetHeader action={<SideSheetClose render={<IconButton aria-label="Close" />}><CloseIcon /></SideSheetClose>}>
      <SideSheetTitle>Filters</SideSheetTitle>
    </SideSheetHeader>
    <SideSheetBody>…</SideSheetBody>
    <SideSheetActions>
      <SideSheetClose render={<Button />}>Apply</SideSheetClose>
    </SideSheetActions>
  </SideSheetContent>
</SideSheet>
```

### Props

**SideSheet**

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `side` | `"right" \| "left"` | `"right"` | The edge it slides in from (and swipes out to). |
| `open / defaultOpen / onOpenChange` | `boolean` |  | Control the sheet. |
| `modal` | `boolean` | `true` | Trap focus and lock page scroll while open. |

**SideSheetHeader**

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `navigation` | `ReactNode` |  | Leading slot, e.g. a back button. |
| `action` | `ReactNode` |  | Trailing slot, usually the close button. |

**SideSheetContent**

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `motion` | `"expressive" \| "standard" \| "fluid" \| "none"` | `theme default` | Motion scheme for this component's transitions. `none` turns animation off. |
| `className` | `string` |  | Extra classes, merged with tailwind-merge. |

### Accessibility

- Opens as a modal `dialog` named by `SideSheetTitle`; focus is trapped inside until it closes.
- Escape, the scrim and a swipe toward the edge all close it; give the close button an `aria-label`.

<a id="table"></a>

## Table

Data tables with sortable headers, selectable rows, numeric columns and a sticky header.

- Install: `npx @grenishrai/expressive add table`
- Group: Containment
- Files: `components/table.tsx`
- Expressive dependencies: `utils`, `styles`
- npm dependencies: none
- Docs: https://expressive.grenishrai.pro/docs/components/table

Tables show records in rows and columns so people can scan, compare and act on them. Headers can sort their column, rows can be selected (pair them with checkboxes), and numeric columns align to the right with tabular figures. Wide tables scroll sideways inside their container instead of the page.

### Usage

```tsx
import { Table, TableBody, TableCell, TableHead, TableHeader, TableRow } from "@/components/expressive/table";

<Table aria-label="Invoices">
  <TableHeader>
    <TableRow>
      <TableHead>Client</TableHead>
      <TableHead numeric sort={sort} onSort={toggleSort}>Amount</TableHead>
    </TableRow>
  </TableHeader>
  <TableBody>
    {rows.map((row) => (
      <TableRow key={row.id} selected={selected.has(row.id)}>
        <TableCell>{row.client}</TableCell>
        <TableCell numeric>{row.amount}</TableCell>
      </TableRow>
    ))}
  </TableBody>
</Table>
```

### With TanStack Table

`Table` only draws: it has no state, so it pairs well with a headless table library. [TanStack Table](https://tanstack.com/table) supplies the logic (sorting, multi-sort, filtering, pagination, selection, column visibility, grouping) and these components render it. Install it with `npm install @tanstack/react-table`.

This example sorts (shift-click a second header to sort by both), selects rows with checkboxes, and pages ten rows at a time. `getToggleSortingHandler()` goes straight into `onSort`, and TanStack's `asc` / `desc` map to the `sort` prop, which sets `aria-sort`.

```tsx
"use client";

import * as React from "react";
import {
  type ColumnDef,
  type RowData,
  type SortingState,
  flexRender,
  getCoreRowModel,
  getPaginationRowModel,
  getSortedRowModel,
  useReactTable,
} from "@tanstack/react-table";
import { Checkbox } from "@/components/expressive/checkbox";
import { IconButton } from "@/components/expressive/icon-button";
import { Table, TableBody, TableCell, TableHead, TableHeader, TableRow } from "@/components/expressive/table";

// Let columns ask for numeric alignment.
declare module "@tanstack/react-table" {
  interface ColumnMeta<TData extends RowData, TValue> {
    numeric?: boolean;
  }
}

type Invoice = { id: string; client: string; status: string; amount: number };

const money = new Intl.NumberFormat("en-US", { style: "currency", currency: "USD" });

const columns: ColumnDef<Invoice>[] = [
  {
    id: "select",
    enableSorting: false,
    header: ({ table }) => (
      <Checkbox
        aria-label="Select all on this page"
        checked={table.getIsAllPageRowsSelected()}
        indeterminate={table.getIsSomePageRowsSelected()}
        onCheckedChange={(checked) => table.toggleAllPageRowsSelected(checked)}
      />
    ),
    cell: ({ row }) => (
      <Checkbox
        aria-label={`Select ${row.original.id}`}
        checked={row.getIsSelected()}
        onCheckedChange={(checked) => row.toggleSelected(checked)}
      />
    ),
  },
  { accessorKey: "id", header: "Invoice" },
  { accessorKey: "client", header: "Client" },
  { accessorKey: "status", header: "Status", enableSorting: false },
  {
    accessorKey: "amount",
    header: "Amount",
    meta: { numeric: true },
    cell: ({ getValue }) => money.format(getValue<number>()),
  },
];

/** TanStack's sort state, in the terms `aria-sort` uses. */
const sortOf = (sorted: false | "asc" | "desc") => (sorted === "asc" ? "ascending" : sorted === "desc" ? "descending" : "none");

export function InvoicesTable({ data }: { data: Invoice[] }) {
  const [sorting, setSorting] = React.useState<SortingState>([]);
  const [rowSelection, setRowSelection] = React.useState({});
  const table = useReactTable({
    data,
    columns,
    state: { sorting, rowSelection },
    onSortingChange: setSorting,
    onRowSelectionChange: setRowSelection,
    getRowId: (row) => row.id,
    getCoreRowModel: getCoreRowModel(),
    getSortedRowModel: getSortedRowModel(),
    getPaginationRowModel: getPaginationRowModel(),
    initialState: { pagination: { pageSize: 10 } },
  });
  const { pageIndex, pageSize } = table.getState().pagination;
  const total = table.getRowCount();

  return (
    <div className="flex flex-col gap-2">
      <Table aria-label="Invoices">
        <TableHeader>
          {table.getHeaderGroups().map((group) => (
            <TableRow key={group.id}>
              {group.headers.map((header) => (
                <TableHead
                  key={header.id}
                  colSpan={header.colSpan}
                  numeric={header.column.columnDef.meta?.numeric}
                  sort={header.column.getCanSort() ? sortOf(header.column.getIsSorted()) : undefined}
                  onSort={header.column.getToggleSortingHandler()}
                >
                  {header.isPlaceholder ? null : flexRender(header.column.columnDef.header, header.getContext())}
                </TableHead>
              ))}
            </TableRow>
          ))}
        </TableHeader>
        <TableBody>
          {table.getRowModel().rows.map((row) => (
            <TableRow key={row.id} selected={row.getIsSelected()}>
              {row.getVisibleCells().map((cell) => (
                <TableCell key={cell.id} numeric={cell.column.columnDef.meta?.numeric}>
                  {flexRender(cell.column.columnDef.cell, cell.getContext())}
                </TableCell>
              ))}
            </TableRow>
          ))}
        </TableBody>
      </Table>

      <div className="flex items-center justify-end gap-2 text-body-medium text-on-surface-variant">
        <span>
          {total === 0 ? 0 : pageIndex * pageSize + 1}–{Math.min((pageIndex + 1) * pageSize, total)} of {total}
        </span>
        <IconButton aria-label="Previous page" disabled={!table.getCanPreviousPage()} onClick={() => table.previousPage()}>
          <ChevronLeftIcon />
        </IconButton>
        <IconButton aria-label="Next page" disabled={!table.getCanNextPage()} onClick={() => table.nextPage()}>
          <ChevronRightIcon />
        </IconButton>
      </div>
    </div>
  );
}
```

- Filtering: add `getFilteredRowModel()` and drive `column.setFilterValue()` or `setGlobalFilter()` from a `TextField` above the table.
- Server data: set `manualSorting`, `manualPagination` and `rowCount`, and fetch when `sorting` or `pagination` changes; the markup stays the same.
- Column visibility: render a `Menu` of `MenuCheckboxItem`s bound to `column.getIsVisible()` and `column.toggleVisibility()`.
- Thousands of rows: page them, or virtualize with TanStack Virtual. Virtual rows are absolutely positioned, so give the body `display: grid` and fixed column widths.

### Props

**Table**

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `variant` | `"outlined" \| "filled" \| "plain"` | `"outlined"` | A bordered surface, a tonal surface, or none. |
| `density` | `"comfortable" \| "compact"` | `"comfortable"` | Row height: 52px or 40px. |
| `stickyHeader` | `boolean` | `false` | Keep the header visible while rows scroll; give the container a max height. |
| `containerProps` | `ComponentProps<"div">` |  | Props for the scrolling wrapper, e.g. `{ className: "max-h-96" }`. |
| `className` | `string` |  | Extra classes, merged with tailwind-merge. |

**TableHead**

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `sort` | `"ascending" \| "descending" \| "none"` |  | Makes the header a sort button and sets `aria-sort`. |
| `onSort` | `(event) => void` |  | Called with the click event when the sort button is pressed; you choose the next direction and sort the rows. TanStack's `getToggleSortingHandler()` fits as is. |
| `numeric` | `boolean` |  | Right-align, to match a numeric column. |

**TableRow**

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `selected` | `boolean` |  | Highlights the row and sets `aria-selected`. |

**TableCell**

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `numeric` | `boolean` |  | Right-align with tabular figures. |

### Accessibility

- A real `<table>`: screen readers announce column headers and each cell's position.
- Name the table with `TableCaption` or `aria-label`.
- Sortable headers are buttons inside the `<th>`, and the column reports its order with `aria-sort`.
- Selection checkboxes need their own labels, e.g. "Select INV-1042".

### Notes

- Sorting, selection and pagination stay in your code: the table renders whatever rows you give it, so it works with any data source or table library.

<a id="alert"></a>

## Alert

Inline info, success, warning and error messages with actions and dismissal.

- Install: `npx @grenishrai/expressive add alert`
- Group: Communication
- Files: `components/alert.tsx`
- Expressive dependencies: `utils`, `styles`
- npm dependencies: none
- Docs: https://expressive.grenishrai.pro/docs/components/alert

Alerts are inline messages that stay on the page until the situation is resolved or dismissed: a failed sync, an expiring plan, an update. Four types set the color and icon. For a passing message use a snackbar or toast; to stop the user until they decide, an alert dialog.

### Usage

```tsx
import { Alert } from "@/components/expressive/alert";

<Alert type="warning" title="Storage almost full" actions={<Button variant="text" size="sm">Manage storage</Button>}>
  You've used 92% of your 15 GB.
</Alert>

<Alert type="error" title="Sync failed" onDismiss={() => setShown(false)}>
  Changes on this device haven't been saved yet.
</Alert>
```

### Props

**Alert**

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `type` | `"info" \| "success" \| "warning" \| "error"` | `"info"` | Color, icon and how urgently it's announced. |
| `title` | `ReactNode` |  | Short summary in bold. |
| `children` | `ReactNode` |  | Details. |
| `icon` | `ReactNode \| null` |  | Replaces the type's icon; `null` removes it. |
| `actions` | `ReactNode` |  | Text buttons under the message; they take the alert's color. |
| `onDismiss` | `() => void` |  | Shows a close button that calls this. |
| `dismissLabel` | `string` | `"Dismiss"` | Accessible name of the close button. |
| `className` | `string` |  | Extra classes, merged with tailwind-merge. |

### Accessibility

- Errors and warnings render `role="alert"` (announced immediately); info and success `role="status"` (announced politely). Override with `role`.
- Render the alert when the condition appears so the announcement happens then; an alert present on page load isn't announced.
- Color isn't the only signal: each type has its own icon, and the title says what happened.

<a id="alert-dialog"></a>

## Alert dialog

A dialog that asks to confirm a consequential action and can't be dismissed by clicking outside.

- Install: `npx @grenishrai/expressive add alert-dialog`
- Group: Communication
- Files: `components/alert-dialog.tsx`
- Expressive dependencies: `utils`, `motion`, `styles`
- npm dependencies: `@base-ui/react`
- Docs: https://expressive.grenishrai.pro/docs/components/alert-dialog

An alert dialog interrupts to confirm a consequential action, like deleting files or discarding a draft. Unlike a regular dialog, clicking outside doesn't close it: the user has to choose. Say what will happen in the description, and label buttons with the outcome ("Delete", not "OK").

### Usage

```tsx
import {
  AlertDialog, AlertDialogActions, AlertDialogClose, AlertDialogContent,
  AlertDialogDescription, AlertDialogTitle, AlertDialogTrigger,
} from "@/components/expressive/alert-dialog";

<AlertDialog>
  <AlertDialogTrigger render={<Button variant="tonal" />}>Delete files</AlertDialogTrigger>
  <AlertDialogContent>
    <AlertDialogTitle>Delete 3 files?</AlertDialogTitle>
    <AlertDialogDescription>They can't be recovered.</AlertDialogDescription>
    <AlertDialogActions>
      <AlertDialogClose render={<Button variant="text" />}>Cancel</AlertDialogClose>
      <AlertDialogClose render={<Button variant="text" />} onClick={deleteFiles}>Delete</AlertDialogClose>
    </AlertDialogActions>
  </AlertDialogContent>
</AlertDialog>
```

### Props

**AlertDialog**

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `open / defaultOpen` | `boolean` |  | Open state. |
| `onOpenChange` | `(open: boolean) => void` |  | Called on open and close. |

**AlertDialogContent**

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `motion` | `"expressive" \| "standard" \| "fluid" \| "none"` | `theme default` | Motion scheme for this component's transitions. `none` turns animation off. |
| `className` | `string` |  | Extra classes, merged with tailwind-merge. |

**AlertDialogTitle, AlertDialogDescription, AlertDialogIcon, AlertDialogActions, AlertDialogTrigger, AlertDialogClose**

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `…` |  |  | Parts; Title and Description are wired to `aria-labelledby` and `aria-describedby`. |

### Accessibility

- Renders `role="alertdialog"`, traps focus, and returns it to the trigger on close.
- Escape still closes it (as Cancel would); an outside click doesn't.
- Always include a cancel action, and keep the description short enough to read before choosing.

<a id="badge"></a>

## Badge

Small dot and numbered badges for icons, tabs and navigation.

- Install: `npx @grenishrai/expressive add badge`
- Group: Communication
- Files: `components/badge.tsx`
- Expressive dependencies: `utils`, `styles`
- npm dependencies: none
- Docs: https://expressive.grenishrai.pro/docs/components/badge

Badges flag new or unread content on an icon. A small 6px dot means "something new"; a numbered badge shows a count, capped at 999+. Pin one to an icon with `BadgeAnchor`, or pass it to a tab.

### Usage

```tsx
import { Badge, BadgeAnchor } from "@/components/expressive/badge";

<BadgeAnchor badge={<Badge count={3} />}>
  <ChatIcon />
</BadgeAnchor>

<IconButton aria-label="Notifications, 8 new">
  <BadgeAnchor badge={<Badge count={8} />}><BellIcon /></BadgeAnchor>
</IconButton>
```

### Props

**Badge**

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `count` | `number \| string` |  | The number to show. Omit it for a small dot. |
| `max` | `number` | `999` | Larger counts show as `999+`. |
| `label` | `string` |  | Accessible text, e.g. "3 unread messages". Without it the badge is hidden from screen readers. |
| `className` | `string` |  | Extra classes, merged with tailwind-merge. |

**BadgeAnchor**

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `badge` | `ReactNode` |  | The badge to pin over the top-right corner of `children` (a 24px icon). |

### Accessibility

- Badges are hidden from screen readers by default, since "3" alone means little. Put the count in the parent's name instead ("Notifications, 8 new"), or pass `label`.
- Error colors stay readable in light and dark themes; don't rely on the badge color alone to carry meaning.

<a id="loading"></a>

## Loading

Loading indicators: circular, wavy, the M3 Expressive shape morph, a spinning shape, bouncing dots and a pulse.

- Install: `npx @grenishrai/expressive add loading`
- Group: Communication
- Files: `components/loading.tsx`
- Expressive dependencies: `shape`, `motion`, `utils`, `styles`
- npm dependencies: none
- Docs: https://expressive.grenishrai.pro/docs/components/loading

Loading indicators show that something is happening. Use `morph`, the M3 Expressive loading indicator, for short waits of a few seconds; `circular` or `wavy` when you can show progress; `shape`, `dots` or `pulse` for lighter, branded moments. For long, measurable tasks prefer a progress bar.

### Usage

```tsx
import { Loading } from "@/components/expressive/loading";

<Loading variant="morph" />                                   // M3 Expressive shape morph
<Loading variant="morph" contained />                          // on a filled container
<Loading variant="circular" label="Loading…" />                 // with text
<Loading variant="wavy" value={progress} aria-label="Upload" /> // determinate
<Loading variant="shape" shape="flower" />                      // one shape spinning
<Loading variant="dots" shape="cookie-4" label="Thinking" />
```

### Props

**Loading**

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `variant` | `"circular" \| "wavy" \| "morph" \| "shape" \| "dots" \| "pulse"` | `"circular"` | Indicator style. |
| `label` | `ReactNode` |  | Visible text; also the accessible name. |
| `labelPosition` | `"end" \| "bottom"` | `"end"` | Where the label sits. |
| `size` | `number` | `48` | Indicator size in px. |
| `value` | `number \| null` | `null` | `circular` and `wavy` only: 0–100 for determinate progress. |
| `shape` | `MaterialShapeName` | `"flower"` | `shape`, `dots` and `pulse`: which shape to draw. |
| `shapes` | `MaterialShapeName[]` | `Compose sequence` | `morph`: shapes to cycle through. Defaults to soft burst → 9-sided cookie → pentagon → pill → sunny → 4-sided cookie → oval. |
| `contained` | `boolean` | `false` | `morph` and `shape`: draw on a filled circular container. |
| `aria-label` | `string` | `"Loading"` | Accessible name when there's no `label`. |

### Accessibility

- Renders `role="progressbar"`, named by `label` (or `aria-label`, defaulting to “Loading”).
- Determinate indicators expose `aria-valuenow` from 0 to 100; indeterminate ones expose no value.
- Indicators keep moving under reduced motion, since the movement is the information, but morphs switch instantly and the morph indicator drops its quarter-turn jumps.

### Notes

- The morph timing matches Compose's LoadingIndicator: a new shape every 650ms on a spring, a quarter turn per morph, and a full rotation every 4.7s.

<a id="progress"></a>

## Progress

Linear (including wavy) and circular progress, determinate or indeterminate.

- Install: `npx @grenishrai/expressive add progress`
- Group: Communication
- Files: `components/progress.tsx`
- Expressive dependencies: `utils`, `styles`
- npm dependencies: `@base-ui/react`
- Docs: https://expressive.grenishrai.pro/docs/components/progress

Progress indicators show that something is happening. Use determinate indicators when you know how far along a task is, indeterminate ones when you don't. The wavy linear style is an M3 Expressive addition for longer, more prominent tasks.

### Usage

```tsx
import { CircularProgress, LinearProgress } from "@/components/expressive/progress";

<LinearProgress value={uploaded} aria-label="Uploading photos" />
<LinearProgress value={uploaded} wavy aria-label="Uploading photos" />
<CircularProgress value={null} aria-label="Loading" />
```

### Props

**LinearProgress**

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `value` | `number \| null` |  | Progress, or `null` for indeterminate. |
| `min / max` | `number` | `0 / 100` | Range of `value`. |
| `wavy` | `boolean` | `false` | Draw the active part as an animated wave. |
| `aria-label` | `string` |  | What is in progress. |

**CircularProgress**

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `value` | `number \| null` |  | Progress, or `null` for indeterminate. |
| `size` | `number` | `48` | Diameter in px. |
| `aria-label` | `string` |  | What is in progress. |

### Accessibility

- Exposes `role="progressbar"` with `aria-valuenow` when determinate, and no value when indeterminate.
- Name it with `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`.

<a id="snackbar"></a>

## Snackbar

One-at-a-time snackbars with an optional action, via useSnackbar().

- Install: `npx @grenishrai/expressive add snackbar`
- Group: Communication
- Files: `components/snackbar.tsx`
- Expressive dependencies: `utils`, `styles`
- npm dependencies: `@base-ui/react`
- Docs: https://expressive.grenishrai.pro/docs/components/snackbar

Snackbars confirm what just happened and can offer one action, like Undo. Only one shows at a time; a new one replaces the current one.

### Usage

```tsx
// app/layout.tsx
import { SnackbarProvider } from "@/components/expressive/snackbar";

<SnackbarProvider>{children}</SnackbarProvider>

// anywhere inside
import { useSnackbar } from "@/components/expressive/snackbar";

const snackbar = useSnackbar();
snackbar.show({ message: "Photo deleted", action: { label: "Undo", onClick: restore } });
```

### Props

**snackbar.show(options)**

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `message` | `ReactNode` |  | What happened. |
| `action` | `{ label: string; onClick: () => void }` |  | One action. Using it also dismisses the snackbar. |
| `closable` | `boolean` | `false` | Show a close button. |
| `timeout` | `number` | `4000 (8000 with an action)` | Milliseconds before it hides. `0` keeps it open. |

**SnackbarProvider**

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `className` | `string` |  | Extra classes, merged with tailwind-merge. |

### Accessibility

- Messages are announced politely through a live region.
- Actionable snackbars stay longer by default so there's time to reach the action.
- Hovering or focusing the snackbar pauses its timer.

<a id="toast"></a>

## Toast

Stacked toasts with titles, type icons, actions and promise states, via useToast().

- Install: `npx @grenishrai/expressive add toast`
- Group: Communication
- Files: `components/toast.tsx`
- Expressive dependencies: `utils`, `motion`, `styles`
- npm dependencies: `@base-ui/react`
- Docs: https://expressive.grenishrai.pro/docs/components/toast

Toasts are notifications that can pile up: each has a title, an optional description, a type icon and an optional action. They stack in a corner, fan out on hover or focus, and can be swiped away. A promise toast shows progress and then the result. For a single brief message, the snackbar is the Material 3 choice.

### Usage

```tsx
import { ToastProvider, useToast } from "@/components/expressive/toast";

// Once, near the root:
<ToastProvider>{children}</ToastProvider>

// Anywhere inside:
const toast = useToast();
toast.success("Changes saved", { description: "Synced across devices." });
toast.error("Couldn't send", { action: { label: "Retry", onClick: retry } });
toast.promise(upload(file), {
  loading: "Uploading…",
  success: (result) => `Uploaded ${result.name}`,
  error: "Upload failed",
});
```

### Props

**ToastProvider**

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `position` | `"bottom-left" \| "bottom-center" \| "bottom-right"` | `"bottom-right"` | Where the stack sits. |
| `limit` | `number` | `3` | How many toasts show at once; older ones fade out. |
| `timeout` | `number` | `5000` | Default ms before a toast dismisses itself. |
| `motion` | `"expressive" \| "standard" \| "fluid" \| "none"` | `theme default` | Motion scheme for this component's transitions. `none` turns animation off. |

**useToast()**

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `show(options)` | `(ToastOptions) => string` |  | Any toast: `title`, `description`, `type`, `action`, `timeout`. Returns its id. |
| `info / success / warning / error` | `(title, options?) => string` |  | Shorthands that set the type and its icon. |
| `promise(promise, states)` | `Promise<T>` |  | A loading toast that becomes `success` or `error`. Each state takes text, a function of the result, or options. |
| `dismiss(id?)` | `(id?: string) => void` |  | Close one toast, or all of them. |

### Accessibility

- Toasts live in a labelled region and are announced politely, without stealing focus.
- F6 moves focus to the stack; while it has focus or the pointer, timers pause and the stack fans out.
- Escape dismisses the focused toast. The close button is for pointer users, so Base UI hides it from screen readers.
- Don't put the only way to do something in a toast: it disappears on its own.

<a id="tooltip"></a>

## Tooltip

Plain and rich tooltips.

- Install: `npx @grenishrai/expressive add tooltip`
- Group: Communication
- Files: `components/tooltip.tsx`
- Expressive dependencies: `utils`, `motion`, `styles`
- npm dependencies: `@base-ui/react`
- Docs: https://expressive.grenishrai.pro/docs/components/tooltip

Plain tooltips briefly name an element, usually an icon button. Rich tooltips add a title, more text and an optional action. Neither should hold information people can't get elsewhere.

### Usage

```tsx
import { RichTooltip, Tooltip, TooltipProvider } from "@/components/expressive/tooltip";

<TooltipProvider>
  <Tooltip content="Search">
    <IconButton aria-label="Search"><SearchIcon /></IconButton>
  </Tooltip>
</TooltipProvider>
```

### Props

**Tooltip**

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `content` | `ReactNode` |  | Tooltip text. |
| `children` | `ReactElement` |  | The trigger. A single element that accepts a ref. |
| `side / align` | `"top" \| "bottom" \| "left" \| "right" / "start" \| "center" \| "end"` | `"top" / "center"` | Placement. |
| `open / defaultOpen / onOpenChange` |  |  | Control the open state. |
| `motion` | `"expressive" \| "standard" \| "fluid" \| "none"` | `theme default` | Motion scheme for this component's transitions. `none` turns animation off. |

**RichTooltip**

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | `ReactNode` |  | Optional title. |
| `actions` | `ReactNode` |  | Text buttons. |

### Accessibility

- Opens on hover and keyboard focus, closes on Escape.
- A tooltip doesn't replace an accessible name: keep `aria-label` on icon buttons.
- Wrap toolbars in TooltipProvider so moving between triggers opens the next tooltip instantly.
